A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same counterfactual-bias certification framework, renamed from QuaCer-B to LLMCert-B. Their text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM certification results on BOLD and Decoding Trust, hyperparameter ablations, case studies, and a human evaluation of its bias detector.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds decoding-parameter ablations, a synthetic confidence-interval coverage experiment, and additional bias-detector evaluation metrics.

M1.justification: The Clopper-Pearson certification procedure, three prefix-generation algorithms, and BOLD/DT bias detectors remain unchanged. Renaming the framework and clarifying its counterfactual scope do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds a synthetic Bernoulli scenario with known success probabilities to evaluate interval coverage. BOLD profession/gender coverage and Decoding Trust racial-stereotype coverage, including the three-group experiment, are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same evaluated models and both comparison baselines: prompting without a prefix and with the unmodified main jailbreak. Newly discussed conformal-prediction and Prompt Risk Control methods are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols vary decoding temperature and top-k and test interval coverage using 50 Bernoulli samples at 11 known probabilities. Bias-detector evaluation adds precision and recall. Existing benchmark sample counts and baseline procedures remain unchanged; newly listed decoding defaults do not establish a change to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 adds temperature and top-k sensitivity analyses; Appendix F adds synthetic interval-coverage validation; Appendix G.1 extends detector error analysis. Earlier sampling/prefix ablations, human-study examples, case studies, and the three-group experiment are retained, making these supplementary extensions.

E5.justification: Appendix F introduces 1,000 repetitions per assumed Bernoulli probability and reports empirical confidence-interval coverage against the nominal 95% level. The original certification confidence level, 50 samples per certificate, and five baseline evaluations remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 is numerically identical, and v2 Table 3's three-group results reappear unchanged in v3 Table 4. Added findings include minor sensitivity to decoding settings, simulated coverage exceeding 95%, and detector precision of 93% with recall of 50%. New Table 2 repeats existing results.

T1.justification: Definition 1, Equation 1, and the mathematical certification argument retain their substance. Explicitly describing the prompt distribution as discrete and changing notation do not alter the existing finite prompt-space formulation. The new coverage simulation adds empirical evidence, not a proof or theorem.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, and contributions explicitly foreground counterfactual bias, and v3 adds the novelty claim that its specifications are the first relational properties for trustworthy LLMs. v2 already studied counterfactual prompts, so the central certification contribution and vulnerability claims remain intact.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly excludes queries where demographic attributes legitimately affect the answer, interprets low detector recall as making unbiased-response bounds optimistic, and proposes an aggregation-based explanation for decoding stability. These qualify and extend existing interpretations without replacing the main conclusions.

D1.justification: Table 3 newly documents decoding temperature 1.0 and top-k 10. Appendix A adds GPL licensing information, model-integration file names, and customization guidance; the reproducibility statement identifies README instructions and human-evaluation files. These improve documentation without establishing changed settings for retained results.

R1.justification: Section 6 and new Appendix H substantially expand positioning against conformal language-model guarantees and Prompt Risk Control, distinguishing their guarantees from relational counterfactual-bias certification. Appendix I adds a broader grounding in fairness concepts and social harms, substantially extending v2's brief treatment.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title, framework name, affiliations, and publication header; tightens prose; and reorganizes the appendices. The former impacts appendix becomes the ethics statement, while practitioner and reproducibility guidance gain dedicated sections. The main section sequence and much of the exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds decoding-sensitivity and coverage plots, a table repeating selected existing results, and decoding rows in the hyperparameter table. Figure 1 names Clopper-Pearson and corrects its caption to unbiased responses. Existing plots and example images are retained, with appendix displays relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through detector precision/recall reporting, decoding checks, coverage validation, practical instructions, and clearer positioning against prior guarantees. These are useful incremental gains; the method and main results remain unchanged. Redundant Table 2, whose caption incorrectly promises baseline columns, is a limited presentation drawback.
